title: 'Check ffmpeg encoders' step passes when only ONE of libvpx/libopus is present, although the remux test needs both
evidence:
grep -E with an alternation exits 0 if any line matches either name, so the `if ! ...` guard never fires when one encoder is missing. packages/meeting-bot/src/capture/record-backend.test.ts:22 invokes ffmpeg with `-c:v libvpx -c:a libopus`, which needs both. Reproduction: `printf ' V..... libvpx
' | grep -E "libvpx|libopus"` exits 0. Result: the intended early ::error:: diagnostic is bypassed and the failure reappears as a confusing test failure.
fix_direction: Check each encoder separately, e.g. `ffmpeg -hide_banner -encoders > enc.txt; for e in libvpx libopus; do grep -qE " $e( |$)" enc.txt || { echo "::error::ffmpeg lacks encoder $e"; exit 1; }; done`. Note libvpx also matches libvpx-vp9 as a prefix; anchor on whitespace to require plain libvpx (VP8) since the test uses `-c:v libvpx`.
